## Current continuation and experience reviews

Follow [OPUS-STAGE-REVIEWS](tasks/OPUS-STAGE-REVIEWS.md): after the current controls/flow polish and at the end of M2, M3 and M4, commission a thorough Opus5.5/high experience review. Substantive findings receive detailed implementation advice, coordinator reconciliation, Sol-authored corrections and affected verification/re-review. Keep the Astra/Sol feature/milestone gate and separate post-M3 Astra critic. The old pause/audit-only boundary is lifted; continue ordinary construction without repeated permission. Menu/subtitle restraint is a project-wide requirement in DELIVERY_AND_ACCEPTANCE, not just a one-off visual fix.

## FND-01 acceptance

1. Strict TypeScript, pinned Vite/Babylon.js and lockfile. Bundled runtime; documented clean install/dev/build/preview/check commands. WebGL 2 support failure is clear.
2. Renderer-independent typed IDs, state, commands/events, fixed-step update and versioned save boundary. Plain serializable state contains no Babylon objects. One content-ID authority reflects the accepted regions/materials/fleet; no competing lore registry.
3. Launchable original richer-cel shallow-ocean foundation with recognizable refuge, island landmark, waterline and player movement. It is visibly an early build. Menu/HUD/controls are usable, not a promise that later campaign content already works.
4. New Game/Continue, safe local save/load and import/export boundary, pause/focus behavior. Invalid/newer/corrupt saves fail without silently overwriting valid progress. Exact migration policy recorded.
5. Meaningful tests exercise save round-trip/invalid data and fixed-step/pause boundaries. Production build and actual browser smoke cover scene loading, ordinary controls, pause and reload if isolated Linux automation is available. Evidence states all gaps; simulation injection does not count as ordinary-input play.
6. Return commit, changed paths, actual checks, evidence locations, proposed contract changes and known gaps. No dependent implementation dispatch by worker. Both independent reviews follow coordinator inspection.

The owner requested an additional dedicated game-design critic near the end. [DESIGN-CRITIC](tasks/DESIGN-CRITIC.md) runs on the full playable campaign at the M3-to-M4 transition, with correction time reserved before release. Primary-source research and the critic procedure passed [paired independent review](reviews/DESIGN-PREP-R1.md) at `c0aa5cb`; it is not a review of the current incomplete game. A fresh non-author Astra xhigh critic examines the actual game, and Sol max implements accepted fixes. Keep the separate Astra/Sol technical acceptance pair.

One main builder owns the first runnable baseline. After reconciliation, split along proven module seams: simulation/progression, renderer/assets/world presentation, and content/UI/audio as appropriate. Assign exclusive paths and one composition owner. Use T3 worktree delegation from a committed baseline for independent checkouts. Integrate small commits and test combined behavior before expanding scope.

M1 carrier validation confirms an explicit M2 obligation: implement player registration of a mobile refuge and ordinary safe/unsafe fallback when that designated craft is disabled or lost. The simplified M1 fixture currently supports static-place refuge IDs and tests pod fallback from an interior/disabled carrier through labelled drills. These are distinct; the fixture cannot satisfy the full mobile-home recovery requirement. Preserve this in the M2 assignment and later full-fleet recovery checks; see [carrier disposition](evidence/M1-CARRIER-INTEGRATION.md).

Construction PRs target `game/siltwake`; the final integration PR targets the appropriate reviewed base/main and makes its planning dependency explicit. Main merge/public hosting are separate owner actions. Routine game-branch integration is authorized after applicable acceptance; the owner explicitly resumed construction and the earlier input pause is over.
